en: As for the body of the Colonel, it is somewhat misleading to state it as “missing,” for it was never reported as such. As far as we know, no one ever claimed it, and its memory does not even live in the bodies of his descendants—if any—in or around Milot. Further, whereas we know what both Christophe and Frederick looked like because both had the wish and the power to have their features engraved for posterity, one of the three faces of Sans Souci may have disappeared forever, at least in its most material form. The royal portrait commissioned by Henry I from Richard Evans, reproduced in many recent books, remains a source that Sans Souci the man has yet to match: there is no known image of the Colonel. In short, because historical traces are inherently uneven, sources are not created equal.
zh: 至于上校的遗体，说它“失踪”有些误导，因为它从未被作为失踪报告过。据我们所知，从来没有人认领过它，它的记忆甚至不曾活在米洛特或其周边他的后裔——如果有的话——的身体里。再者，我们知道克里斯托夫和腓特烈长什么样，因为两人都有愿望、也有权力把自己的容貌铭刻下来传给后世；而“无忧”的三副面孔之一，却可能永远消失了，至少在其最物质的形态上。亨利一世委托理查德·埃文斯绘制的皇家肖像，被许多新近书籍复制，它至今没有一份关于桑苏西本人的同类史料与之相称：上校没有任何已知画像。简言之，因为历史痕迹天生不均，史料并非生而平等。

en: But if lived inequalities yield unequal historical power, they do so in ways we have yet to determine. The distribution of historical power does not necessarily replicate the inequalities (victories and setbacks, gains and losses) lived by the actors. Historical power is not a direct reflection of a past occurrence, or a simple sum of past inequalities measured from an actor’s perspective or from the standpoint of any “objective” standard, even at the first moment. The French superiority in artillery, the strategic superiority of Sans Souci, and the political superiority of Christophe can all be demonstrated, but no such demonstration would enable us to predict their relative significance then and now. Similarly, sources do not encapsulate the whole range of significance of the occurrences to which they testify.
zh: 但是，即便亲历的不平等产生了不均的历史权力，其方式也是我们尚待确定的。历史权力的分配，未必复制行动者所亲历的不平等（胜利与挫折、得与失）。历史权力不是某一过去事件的直接反映，也不是从行动者视角或任何“客观”标准立场衡量的过去不平等的简单加总——即便在第一个时刻也是如此。法国人在火炮上的优势、桑苏西在战略上的优势、克里斯托夫在政治上的优势，都可以被证明，但任何这样的证明都不能让我们预测它们在当时和如今的相对意义。同样，史料并不包纳它们所见证的事件的全部意义范围。

en: Further, the outcome itself does not determine in any linear way how an event or a series of events enters into history. The French expeditionary forces lost the Haitian war. (They thought they did, and they did.) Similarly, Colonel Sans Souci was the loser and Christophe the ultimate winner both politically and militarily within the black camp. Yet the papers preserved by General Donatien Rochambeau (Leclerc’s successor as commander of the French expedition) show more than fifty entries about French general Fressinet in spite of the fact that Fressinet was, by anyone’s standard, a fairly minor figure in the Saint-Domingue campaigns. In comparison, there are eleven entries about Christophe, whom we know gave both Leclerc and Rochambeau much more to think about than Fressinet ever did. Sans Souci, in turn—who came close to upsetting the plans of both the French and colonial officers and indeed forced both to change tactics in mid-course—received a single entry.
zh: 再者，结果本身并不以任何线性方式决定一个事件或一系列事件如何进入历史。法国远征军输掉了海地战争。（他们以为自己输了，他们也确实输了。）同样，在黑人阵营内部，无论从政治还是军事上，桑苏西上校都是失败者，克里斯托夫是最终赢家。然而，多纳西安·罗尚博将军（勒克莱尔之后法国远征军的继任指挥官）保存的文件中，关于法国将军弗雷西内的条目有五十多条，尽管以任何标准衡量，弗雷西内在圣多明各战役中都是个相当次要的人物。相比之下，关于克里斯托夫的条目只有十一条，而我们知道，克里斯托夫让勒克莱尔和罗尚博操心的程度，远非弗雷西内所能及。至于桑苏西——他几乎打乱了法国军官和殖民军官双方的计划，并确实迫使双方中途改变战术——只得到一条记载。

en: Thus the presences and absences embodied in sources (artifacts and bodies that turn an event into fact) or archives (facts collected, thematized, and processed as documents and monuments) are neither neutral or natural. They are created. As such, they are not mere presences and absences, but mentions or silences of various kinds and degrees. By silence, I mean an active and transitive process: one “silences” a fact or an individual as a silencer silences a gun. One engages in the practice of silencing. Mentions and silences are thus active, dialectical counterparts of which history is the synthesis. Almost every mention of Sans Souci, the palace, the very resilience of the physical structure itself, effectively silences Sans Souci, the man, his political goals, his military genius.
zh: 因此，体现在史料（把事件转化为事实的人工制品与身体）或档案（被收集、主题化并加工为文献与纪念碑的事实）中的在场与缺席，既非中性，也非自然。它们是被创造的。正因如此，它们不只是在场与缺席，而是各种类型、各种程度的提及或沉默。我所说的沉默，是一个主动的、及物的过程：人们“使”一个事实或一个人“沉默”，正如消音器使枪声沉默。人们从事的是使……沉默的实践。提及与沉默因而是主动的、辩证的对立面，历史则是它们的综合。几乎每一次对无忧宫这座宫殿的提及——乃至物质结构本身的坚韧存续——都实际上使人再也听不到桑苏西这个人、他的政治目标和他的军事才干。

en: Inequalities experienced by the actors lead to uneven historical power in the inscription of traces. Sources built upon these traces in turn privilege some events over others, not always the ones privileged by the actors. Sources are thus instances of inclusion, the other face of which is, of course, what is excluded. This may now be obvious enough to those of us who have learned (though more recently than we care to remember) that sources imply choices. But the conclusion we tend to draw that some occurrences have the capacity (a physical one, I would insist) to enter history and become “fact” at the first stage while others do not is much too general, and ultimately useless in its ecumenical form. That some peoples and things are absent of history, lost, as it were, to the possible world of knowledge, is much less relevant to the historical practice than the fact that some peoples and things are absent in history, and that this absence itself is constitutive of the process of historical production.
zh: 行动者所经历的不平等，导致铭刻痕迹时的历史权力不均。建立在这些痕迹之上的史料，反过来又偏重某些事件而非另一些——未必是行动者所偏重的那些。史料因而是“纳入”的实例，其另一面当然是被排除者。对我们这些已经懂得（尽管懂得的时间比我们愿意承认的要晚）史料意味着选择的人来说，这一点如今也许足够明显。但我们倾向于得出的结论——某些事件有能力（我要强调，是物质上的能力）在第一阶段进入历史、成为“事实”，而另一些则不能——太过笼统，其放之四海的形式最终毫无用处。某些群体和事物游离于历史之外（absent of history），仿佛落在可能被认识的范围之外；对历史实践而言，比这更重要的是另一个事实：某些民族和事物在历史之中缺席（absent in history），而这种缺席本身正是历史生产过程的构成性部分。

en: Silences are inherent in history because any single event enters history with some of its constituting parts missing. Something is always left out while something else is recorded. There is no perfect closure of any event, however one chooses to define the boundaries of that event. Thus whatever becomes fact does so with its own inborn absences, specific to its production. In other words, the very mechanisms that make any historical recording possible also ensure that historical facts are not created equal. They reflect differential control of the means of historical production at the very first engraving that transforms an event into a fact.

Silences of this kind show the limits of strategies that imply a more accurate reconstitution of the past, and therefore the production of a “better” history, simply by an enlargement of the empirical base.

To be sure, the continuous enlargement of the physical boundaries of historical production is useful and necessary. The turn toward hitherto neglected sources (e.g., diaries, images, bodies) and the emphasis on unused facts (e.g., facts of gender, race, and class, facts of the life cycle, facts of resistance) are pathbreaking developments. My point is that when these tactical gains are made to dictate strategy they lead, at worst, to a neo-empiricist enterprise and, at best, to an unnecessary restriction of the battleground for historical power.
zh: 沉默内在于历史，因为任何单个事件进入历史时，都缺失了它的某些构成部分。总有一些东西被遗漏，另一些被记录。无论人们如何界定一个事件的边界，都不存在对它的完美闭合。因此，任何成为事实的东西，都带着它与生俱来的、为其生产所特有的缺席。换句话说，正是使任何历史记录成为可能的那些机制，也确保了历史事实并非生而平等。它们反映了在把事件转化为事实的最初铭刻中，对历史生产手段的差别化控制。
这类沉默显示了某些策略的局限：那些策略以为，仅凭扩大经验基础，就能更准确地重建过去，从而生产出一部“更好的”历史。
诚然，不断扩大历史生产的物质边界是有用且必要的。转向此前被忽视的史料（如日记、图像、身体），强调未被使用的事实（如性别、种族、阶级的事实，生命周期的事实，抵抗的事实），都是开创性的进展。我的论点是：当这些战术收获被用来支配战略时，它们最坏会导致一种新经验主义事业，最好也只是对历史权力战场的不必要限制。

en: As sources fill the historical landscape with their facts, they reduce the room available to other facts. Even if we imagine the landscape to be forever expandable, the rule of interdependence implies that new facts cannot emerge in a vacuum. They will have to gain their right to existence in light of the field constituted by previously created facts. They may dethrone some of these facts, erase or qualify others. The point remains that sources occupy competing positions in the historical landscape. These positions themselves are inherently imbued with meaning since facts cannot be created meaningless. Even as an ideal recorder, the chronicler necessarily produces meaning and, therefore, silences.
zh: 当史料用它们的事实填满历史景观时，它们就减少了其他事实可用的空间。即便我们想象这片景观可以永远扩展，相互依存规则也意味着新事实不能在真空中出现。它们必须依据先前创造的事实所构成的场域，来赢得自己的存在权。它们可能废黜其中一些事实，抹去或限定另一些。关键在于，史料在历史景观中占据着相互竞争的位置。这些位置本身天生充满意义，因为事实不可能被创造得毫无意义。即便作为一个理想的记录者，编年记录者也必然生产意义，因而也生产沉默。

en: The tenets of the distinction between chronicler and narrator are well known.

The chronicler provides a play-by-play account of every event he witnesses, the narrator describes the life of an entity, person, thing, or institution. The chronicler deals with discrete chunks of time united only by his record-keeping; the narrator deals with a continuity provided by the life span of the entity described. The chronicler describes only events that he witnessed; the narrator can tell stories both about what he saw and what he learned to be true from others. The chronicler does not know the end of the story—indeed, there is no point to the story; the narrator knows the full story. The speech of the chronicler is akin to that of a radio announcer giving a play-by-play account of a sports game; the speech of the narrator is akin to that of a storyteller.
zh: 编年记录者与叙述者之分的要旨是众所周知的。

编年记录者按发生次序实况记录他所见的每一件事；叙述者则描述一个实体、人、物或制度的生命。编年记录者处理的是离散的时间块，仅靠他的记录保存才联结起来；叙述者处理的则是由所描述实体的生命跨度提供的连续性。编年记录者只描述他亲眼见证的事件；叙述者既能讲他亲眼所见，也能讲他从他人那里得知为真的事。编年记录者不知道故事的结局——的确，还谈不上有什么贯穿始终的主旨；叙述者知道完整的故事。编年记录者的言说，类似于电台播音员对一场体育比赛作逐球实况解说；叙述者的言说，则类似于讲故事的人。

en: Even if we admit that distinction as couched, silences are inherent in the chronicle. The sportscaster’s account is a play-by-play description but only of the occurrences that matter to the game. Even if it is guided mainly by the seriality of occurrences, it tends to leave out from the series witnesses, participants, and events considered generally as marginal. The audience enters primarily when it is seen as influencing the players. Players on the bench are left out. Players in the field are mentioned mainly when they capture the ball, or at least when they try to capture it or are meant to do so. Silences are necessary to the account, for if the sportscaster told us every “thing” that happened at each and every moment, we would not understand anything. If the account was indeed fully comprehensive of all facts it would be incomprehensible. Further, the selection of what matters, the dual creation of mentions and silences, is premised on the understanding of the rules of the game by broadcaster and audience alike. In short, play-by-play accounts are restricted in terms of what may enter them and in terms of the order in which these elements may enter.
zh: 即便我们接受上述区分，沉默也内在于编年记录。体育解说员按进程作实况播报，但只描述对比赛要紧的事件。即便它主要由事件的先后顺序引导，它也倾向于把通常被视为边缘的见证者、参与者和事件排除在序列之外。观众主要在被认为影响球员时才进入记述。替补席上的球员被略去。场上球员主要在他们抢到球、或至少试图抢球或应当抢球时才被提及。沉默对记述是必要的，因为如果解说员把每一时刻发生的每一“件”事都告诉我们，我们将什么都听不懂。如果记述真的包罗所有事实，它将不可理解。再者，对何者为要紧的选择——提及与沉默的双重创造——以播音员和观众双方对比赛规则的理解为前提。简言之，跟随比赛进程的实况播报在何者可以进入、以及这些要素以何种顺序进入两方面，都受到限制。

en: What is true of play-by-play accounts is no less true of notary records, business accounts, population censuses, parish registers. Historians familiar with the plantation records that inscribe the daily life of Caribbean slaves are well aware that births are under-reported in these records.

Planters or overseers often preferred not to register the existence of a black baby whose survival was unlikely, given the high incidence of infant mortality. Temporary omission made more sense: it could be corrected if the child survived beyond a certain age.
zh: 按进程作实况播报的道理，同样适用于公证记录、商业账目、人口普查、教区登记簿。熟悉那些铭刻加勒比奴隶日常生活的种植园记录的历史学家很清楚，这些记录中出生人数被少报了。
鉴于婴儿死亡率之高，种植园主或监工往往宁愿不登记一个存活希望渺茫的黑人婴儿的存在。暂时略去更合理：如果孩子活过一定年龄，可以再补正。

en: We are not dealing here with a case in which technical or ideological blinders skewed the reporting of the chronicler. It is not as if these lives and deaths were missed by negligence. Nor were they inconsequential to the chronicler: pregnancies and births considerably affected the amount of available labor, the linchpin of the slave system. Masters were not even trying to conceal these births. Rather, both births and deaths were actively silenced in the records for a combination of practical reasons inherent in the reporting itself. To be sure, slavery and racism provided the context within which these silences occurred, but in no way were the silences themselves the direct products of ideology. They made sense in terms of the reporting, in terms of the logic of its accounting procedures. In short, the chronicler-accountant is no less passive than the chronicler-sportscaster. As Emile Benveniste reminds us, the census taker is always a
—and not only because of a lucky play of etymology: he who counts heads always silences facts and voices.
Silences are inherent in the creation of sources, the first moment of historical production.
zh: 我们这里处理的，并不是技术或意识形态造成的视野局限扭曲了编年记录者报告的情形。并不是说这些生与死因疏忽而被漏掉。它们对编年记录者也并非无关紧要：怀孕和出生相当程度地影响可用劳动力的数量，而劳动力是奴隶制的关键。主人甚至不曾试图隐瞒这些出生。毋宁说，出生和死亡都因报告本身固有的一系列实际理由，在记录中被主动沉默了。诚然，奴隶制和种族主义提供了这些沉默发生于其中的语境，但沉默本身绝不是意识形态的直接产物。它们就报告而言、就其核算程序的逻辑而言，是说得通的。简言之，编年记录者—会计，并不比编年记录者—体育解说员更被动。正如埃米尔·邦弗尼斯特提醒我们的，人口普查员（census taker）总也是一位
（censor）——这不仅是因为词源上的巧妙巧合：清点人头的人，总是使事实和声音沉默。
沉默内在于史料的创造，即历史生产的第一个时刻。

en: Unequal control over historical production obtains also in the second moment of historical production, the making of archives and documents. Of course, sources and documents can emerge simultaneously and some analysts conflate the two.

My own insistence on distinguishing a moment of fact-assembly from that of fact-creation is meant first to emphasize that uneven historical power obtains even before any work of classification by non-participants. Slave plantation records entered history as sources with the added value of the inequalities that made them possible long before they were classified into archives. Second, I want to insist that the kind of power used in the creation of sources is not necessarily the same that allows the creation of archives.
zh: 对历史生产的不均控制，也存在于历史生产的第二个时刻，即档案与文献的制造。当然，史料与文献可能同时出现，一些分析者把两者混为一谈。
我坚持区分事实集结的时刻与事实创造的时刻，首先是为了强调：早在非参与者进行任何分类工作之前，不均的历史权力就已经存在。奴隶种植园记录作为史料进入历史时，带着使它们成为可能的那些不平等的附加值，远早于它们被分类编入档案。其次，我要坚持：用于创造史料的那种权力，未必就是允许创造档案的那种权力。

en: By archives, I mean the institutions that organize facts and sources and condition the possibility of existence of historical statements. Archival power determines the difference between a historian, amateur or professional, and a charlatan.
zh: 我所说的档案，是指组织事实与史料、并制约历史陈述存在之可能性的那些制度。档案权力决定了历史学家——无论业余还是职业——与江湖骗子之间的区别。

en: Archives assemble. Their assembly work is not limited to a more or less passive act of collecting. Rather, it is an active act of production that prepares facts for historical intelligibility. Archives set up both the substantive and formal elements of the narrative. They are the institutionalized sites of mediation between the sociohistorical process and the narrative about that process. They enforce the constraints on “debatability” we noted earlier with Appadurai: they convey authority and set the rules for credibility and interdependence; they help select the stories that matter.
zh: 档案进行集结。它们的集结工作不限于或多或少被动的收集行为。毋宁说，它是一种主动的生产行为，整理事实，使它们能够为历史叙述所理解。档案既设定叙述的实质要素，也设定其形式要素。它们是社会历史过程与关于该过程的叙述之间制度化的中介场所。它们执行上文援引阿帕杜莱时提到的对“可争辩性”的约束：它们传递权威，设定可信度与相互依存的规则；它们帮助挑选要紧的故事。

en: So conceived, the category covers competing institutions with various conditions of existence and various modes of labor organization. It includes not only the libraries or depositories sponsored by states and foundations, but less visible institutions that also sort sources to organize facts, according to themes or periods, into documents to be used and monuments to be explored. In that sense, a tourist guide, a museum tour, an archaeological expedition, or an auction at Sotheby’s can perform as much an archival role as the Library of Congress.

The historical guild or, more properly, the rules that condition academic history perform similar archival duties. These rules enforce constraints that belie the romantic image of the professional historian as an independent artist or isolated artisan. The historian is never alone even within the most obscure corner of the archive: the encounter with the document is also an encounter with the guild even for the amateur.
zh: 如此构想，这一范畴涵盖了具有各种存在条件、各种劳动组织方式的相互竞争的制度。它不仅包括国家和基金会资助的图书馆或保管库，也包括不那么显眼的制度——它们同样整理史料，按主题或时期把事实组织为可供使用的文献和可供探索的纪念碑。在这个意义上，一位导游、一次博物馆参观、一次考古发掘，或苏富比的一场拍卖，都能像国会图书馆一样发挥档案作用。
历史行会——或者更准确地说，制约学院史学的那些规则——履行着类似的档案职责。这些规则执行的约束，戳穿了职业历史学家作为独立艺术家或孤立匠人的浪漫形象。历史学家从不孤单，即便在档案最晦暗的角落：与文献的相遇，也是与行会的相遇，即便对业余者亦然。

en: In short, the making of archives involves a number of selective operations: selection of producers, selection of evidence, selection of themes, selection of procedures—which means, at best the differential ranking and, at worst, the exclusion of some producers, some evidence, some themes, some procedures. Power enters here both obviously and surreptitiously. Jean-Baptiste Sans Souci was silenced not only because some narrators may have consciously chosen not to mention him but primarily because most writers followed the acknowledged rules of their time.
zh: 简言之，档案的制造涉及一系列选择性操作：选择生产者、选择证据、选择主题、选择程序——这意味着，最好的情况下是对某些生产者、某些证据、某些主题、某些程序的差别化排序，最坏的情况下则是排除。权力在这里既明显又隐蔽地进入。让-巴蒂斯特·桑苏西之所以从叙述中淡去，不仅因为一些叙述者可能有意识地选择不提他，更主要是因为大多数作家遵循了他们那个时代公认的规则。

en: Silences in the Historical Narrative
zh: 历史叙述中的沉默

en: The dialectics of mentions and silences obtain also at the third moment of the process, when events that have become facts (and may have been processed through archives) are retrieved. Even if we assume instances of pure historical “narrativity,” that is, accounts that describe an alleged past in a way analogous to a sportscaster’s play-by-play description of a game, even if we postulate a recording angel—with no stakes in the story—who would dutifully note all that was mentioned and collected, any subsequent narrative (or any corpus of such narratives) would demonstrate to us that retrieval and recollection proceed unequally. Occurrences equally noted, and supposedly not yet subject to interpretation in the most common sense of the word, exhibit in the historical corpus an unequal frequency of retrieval, unequal (factual) weight, indeed unequal degrees of factualness. Some facts are recalled more often than others; some strings of facts are recalled with more empirical richness than others even in play-by-play accounts.
zh: 提及与沉默的辩证法，也存在于这一过程的第三个时刻，即已成为事实（并可能已经过档案处理）的事件被提取之时。即便我们假定存在纯粹历史“叙述性”（narrativity）的实例——也就是以类似体育解说员跟随一场比赛进程进行实况播报的方式，描述某个所谓过去的记述；即便我们设定一位记录天使——与故事毫无利害瓜葛——会尽责地记下所有被提及和被收集的东西，任何随后的叙述（或此类叙述的任何总体）都会向我们表明：提取与回忆是不均等地进行的。那些被同样记录下来、并且据信尚未受到该词最常见意义上的解释的事件，在历史总体中却呈现出不同的被提取频率、不同的（事实）分量，乃至不同的事实性程度。有些事实比其他事实更常被回忆；即便在逐项实况记述中，有些事实串也比另一些以更丰富的经验内容被回忆。

en: Every fact recorded in my narrative of the Sans Souci story is part of the available record in relatively accessible form since I have used only sources available in multiple copies: memoirs, published accounts, so-called “secondary” sources—that is, material already produced as history. But the frequency with which they appear in the total corpus from which the narrative was drawn varies. So does the material weight of mention, that is, the sheer empirical value of the string within which any single fact is enmeshed.
zh: 我关于桑苏西故事的叙述中记录的每一个事实，都以相对容易获取的形式存在于现存记录之中，因为我只使用了有多个副本可得的史料：回忆录、已刊行的记述、所谓“二手”史料——也就是已经作为历史被生产出来的材料。但它们出现在叙述所取材的整批文献中的频率各不相同。提及的物质分量也是如此，也就是任何单个事实所嵌入其中的那个事实串的纯粹经验价值。

en: That Colonel Sans Souci was not the leader of an impromptu or marginal rebel band but an early leader in the slave uprising and, later, a high-ranking officer of Louverture’s army turned dissident has been a constant fact within the published record from the late eighteenth century to our times.

But that fact remained largely unused until recently: its frequency of retrieval was low, its empirical elaboration defective in terms of the information already available in that corpus. Sans Souci was most often alluded to without mention of grade or origins, without even a first name, all available facts within the corpus. Little was said of the size of his troops, of the details of his death, of his few stated positions.
Yet there was enough to sketch a picture of Sans Souci, even if a very fleeting one, certainly not as elaborate as that of Christophe.
zh: 桑苏西上校并非一支临时拼凑或边缘叛军的首领，而是奴隶起义的早期领袖之一，后来又是卢维杜尔军队中一名转而持异议的高级军官——从十八世纪末直到我们的时代，这一直是已刊行记录中的一个恒常事实。
但这一事实在不久之前基本未被使用：它很少被提取出来；即便有所提及，所用材料也比已有文献能提供的少。人们提及桑苏西时，大多不提他的军衔或出身，甚至不提他的名字——而这些全都是该总体中现成的事实。关于他部队的规模、他死亡的细节、他为数不多的公开立场，都鲜有述及。
然而，现有材料足以勾勒出桑苏西的一幅画像，哪怕极为转瞬即逝，当然远不如克里斯托夫的那幅详尽。

en: Still, materials of that sort had to re-enter the corpus, so to speak, quite slowly and in restricted ways—for instance, as part of a catalogue of documents within which they remained more or less inconspicuous.
Only in the 1980s have they surfaced as (re)discoveries in their own right within a narrative.

Thus, to many readers who had access to most of this corpus and who may or may not have different stakes in the narrative, the extent of Sans Souci’s political dissidence—if not that of his existence—is likely to be apprehended as “news.” So is (for a different group of readers, overlapping—and as substantial as—the first one) the suggestion that the palace at Milot may have been modeled after the palace at Potsdam to an extent still undetermined.
zh: 然而，这类材料不得不说是相当缓慢地、以受限的方式重新进入总体的——例如，作为一份文献目录的一部分，在其中它们或多或少不引人注目。
直到1980年代，它们才在叙述中作为值得单独提及的（重新）发现浮现出来。
因此，对许多能够接触到这一总体大部分内容、对叙述未必怀有相同利害的读者来说，桑苏西的政治异议究竟达到什么程度，甚至有过桑苏西这么一个人——很可能被当作“新闻”来理解。同样如此的还有（对另一群读者而言，这群人与前一群重叠，且规模相当）这样一种提示：米洛特宫可能在某个尚不确定的程度上仿照了波茨坦宫。

en: Now, the individuals who constructed this corpus came from various times and backgrounds, sought to offer various interpretations of the Haitian Revolution, and passed at times opposite value judgments on either the revolution itself or Christophe. Given these conflicting viewpoints, what explains the greater frequency of certain silences in the corpus?
zh: 然而，构建这一总体的个人来自不同时代和背景，试图对海地革命提出各种解释，有时对革命本身或克里斯托夫作出相反的价值判断。鉴于这些相互冲突的观点，该如何解释某些沉默在总体中更高的出现频率？

en: Let us go back to the actual practice of an Ideal Chronicler. Our description of that practice suggests that play-by-play accounts and even inventory lists are restricted, not only in terms of the occurrences they register, but also in terms of the order in which these occurrences are registered. In other words, no chronicle can avoid a minimal structure of narration, a movement that gives it some sense. That structure, barely visible in the typical chronicle, becomes fundamental to the narrative proper.
zh: 让我们回到一位理想编年记录者的实际实践。我们对那种实践的描述表明，逐项实况记述乃至清单目录都受到限制，不仅在它们登记的事件方面，也在这些事件被登记的顺序方面。换句话说，任何编年记录都无法避免一种最低限度的叙述结构，一种赋予它某种意义的运动。这种结构在典型的编年记录中几乎不可见，却成为严格意义上的叙述的根本。

en: Historical narratives are premised on previous understandings, which are themselves premised on the distribution of archival power. In the case of Haitian historiography, as in the case of most Third World countries, these previous understandings have been profoundly shaped by Western conventions and procedures. First, the writing and reading of Haitian historiography implies literacy and formal access to a Western—primarily French—language and culture, two prerequisites that already exclude the majority of Haitians from direct participation in its production. Most Haitians are illiterate and unilingual speakers of Haitian, a French-based Creole. Only a few members of the already tiny elite are native bilingual speakers of French and Haitian. The first published memoirs and histories of the revolution were written almost exclusively in French. So were most of the written traces (letters, proclamations) that have become primary documents. Currently, the vast majority of history books about Saint-Domingue/Haiti is written in French, with a substantial minority of those published in France itself. The first full-length history book (and for that matter the first full-length non-fiction book) written in Haitian Creole is my own work on the revolution, which dates from 1977.
zh: 历史叙述以既有理解为前提，而这些既有理解本身又以档案权力的分配为前提。就海地史学而言，如同大多数第三世界国家一样，这些既有理解深受西方惯例与程序的塑造。首先，海地史学的写作与阅读意味着识字，并意味着对一种西方——主要是法国——语言文化的正规接触，这两个先决条件已经把大多数海地人排除在其生产的直接参与之外。大多数海地人不识字，是海地语的单语使用者，那是一种以法语为基础的克里奥尔语。本就极小的精英阶层中，只有少数成员是以法语和海地语为母语的双语者。革命最早的已刊行回忆录和史著几乎全是用法语写成的。成为第一手文献的大多数文字痕迹（信件、公告）也是如此。目前，关于圣多明各/海地的史书绝大多数用法语写成，其中相当一部分在法国本土出版。第一部用海地克里奥尔语写成的足本史书（就此而言也是第一部足本非虚构著作），是我本人关于革命的研究，出版于1977年。

en: Second, regardless of their training and the degree to which they may be considered members of a guild, Haitian and foreign narrators aim to conform to guild practice. The division between guild historians and amateurs is, of course, premised on a particular Western-dominated practice. In the Haitian case, few if any individuals make a living writing history. Haitian historians have included physicians, lawyers, journalists, businessmen, bureaucrats and politicians, high school teachers and clergymen. Status as historian is not conferred by an academic doctoral degree but by a mixture of publications that conform to a large extent to the standards of the Western guild and active participation in ongoing historical debates. Previous understandings here include an acknowledgment of the now global academic division of labor as shaped by the particular history of Western Europe. Just as sportscasters assume an audience’s limited knowledge of the players (who is who, what are the two sides), so do historians build their narrative on the shoulders of previous ones. The knowledge that narrators assume about their audience limits both their use of the archives and the context within which their story finds significance. To contribute to new knowledge and to add new significance, the narrator must both acknowledge and contradict the power embedded in previous understandings.
zh: 其次，无论受训背景如何、无论他们在多大程度上可被视为行会成员，海地和外国的叙述者都力求符合行会实践。行会历史学家与业余者之间的划分，当然以一种特定的西方主导的实践为前提。在海地的情况下，几乎没有人靠写历史谋生。海地历史学家中有医生、律师、记者、商人、官僚和政客、中学教师和神职人员。历史学家的身份不是由学术博士学位授予的，而是由两方面的混合授予的：在很大程度上符合西方行会标准的出版物，以及对正在进行的历史论争的积极参与。这里的既有理解包括对如今全球学术分工的承认，这种分工由西欧的特殊历史所塑造。正如体育解说员假定观众对球员所知有限（谁是谁、双方是哪两队），历史学家也把自己的叙述建立在前人叙述的肩膀上。叙述者对读者知识的假定，既限制了他们对档案的使用，也限制了他们的故事在其中获得意义的语境。要贡献新知识、增添新意义，叙述者必须既承认又反驳嵌入既有理解中的权力。

en: This chapter itself exemplifies the point. My narrative of the Haitian Revolution assumed both a certain way of reading history and the reader’s greater knowledge of French than of Haitian history. Whether or not these assumptions were correct, they reflect a presumption about the unevenness of historical power. But if they were correct, the narrative had to present an overview of the last years of the Haitian Revolution. Otherwise, the story of Sans Souci would not make sense to most readers. I did not feel the need to underscore that Haiti is in the Caribbean and that Afro-American slavery had been going on in the Caribbean for exactly three centuries when these events occurred. These mentions would have added to the empirical weight of the narrative, but the story still made sense without them. Further, I assumed that most of my readers knew these facts. Still, expecting many of my readers to be North American undergraduates, I took the precaution of inserting throughout the text some clues about Haiti’s topography and its general history. I did not report that Toussaint’s capture (which I qualified as an entrapment) occurred on June 7, 1802, because the exact date did not seem to matter much in the narrative. But if I had done so I would have used, as I do now, the Christian calendar, the year indexation system the West inherited from Dionysius Exiguus rather than, say, an oriental system. Nowhere in this text do I use the

(the system that indexed months and years in most of the primary documents of this story) because it did not prevail in post-revolutionary narratives and lost, therefore, its archival power. Even individuals who were forced to learn its correspondence with Dionysius’s system at an early age (as I was in school) would take some time to ascertain that “le 18 prairial de l’an dix” was indeed June 7, 1802. In short, I bowed to some rules, inherited from a history of uneven power, to ensure the accessibility of my narrative.
zh: 本章本身就例证了这一点。我关于海地革命的叙述，既假定了某种阅读历史的方式，也假定了读者对法国史的了解多于对海地史的了解。无论这些假定是否正确，它们都反映了对历史权力不均的一种预设。但如果它们是正确的，叙述就必须概述海地革命的最后几年。否则，桑苏西的故事对大多数读者来说就讲不通。我不觉得有必要强调海地位于加勒比地区，也不觉得有必要强调这些事件发生时，美洲非洲裔奴隶制在加勒比已整整进行了三个世纪。这些提及会增加叙述的经验分量，但没有它们故事依然讲得通。再者，我假定我的大多数读者知道这些事实。不过，考虑到我的许多读者会是北美本科生，我还是采取了预防措施，在全文中穿插了一些关于海地地形和总体历史的线索。我没有报告杜桑的被捕（我把它定性为一场诱捕）发生在1802年6月7日，因为确切日期在叙述中似乎无关紧要。但如果我要报告，我就会像现在这样使用基督教历法，即西方从小狄奥尼修斯（Dionysius Exiguus）那里继承的纪年体系，而不是比如某种东方体系。本文任何地方都没有使用共和历（calendrier républicain，即这个故事的大多数第一手文献用来标记月年的体系），因为它没有在革命后的叙述中通行，因而失去了它的档案权力。即便是从小被迫学习它与狄奥尼修斯体系对应关系的人（我在学校就是如此），也要花些时间才能确认“le 18 prairial de l’an dix”（共和十年牧月十八日）确实是1802年6月7日。简言之，我屈从了一些从权力不均的历史中继承来的规则，以确保我的叙述可以被理解。

en: Thus, in many ways, my account followed a conventional line—but only up to a certain point because of my treatment of Sans Souci. Until now indeed, the combined effect of previous understandings about plot structures and common empirical knowledge resulted in a partial silencing of the life and death of the Colonel. Players have been distributed according to the major leagues, and the event-units of Haitian history have been cut in slices that cannot be easily modified. Thus the war within the war has been subsumed within accounts of the war between the French and the colonial troops, rarely (if ever) detailed as a narrative in its own right. In that sense, indeed, it never constituted a complete sequence, a play-by-play account of any “thing.” Rather, its constituting events were retrieved as marginal subparts of other accounts, and the life and death of Sans Souci himself as a smaller segment of these subparts. To unearth Colonel Sans Souci as more than a negligible figure within the story of Haiti’s emergence, I chose to add a section that recast his story as a separate account after the chronological sketch of the revolution. This was a choice based on both possible procedures and assessment of my readers’ knowledge. That choice acknowledges power, but it also introduces some dissidence by setting up the war within the war as a historical topic.
zh: 因此，在许多方面，我的记述遵循了一条常规路线——但由于我对桑苏西的处理，只到某一点为止。的确，迄今为止，关于情节结构的既有理解与常识性经验知识的共同作用，导致了对上校生与死的部分沉默化。球员已按大联盟分配，海地历史的事件单元已被切成不易更改的片块。因此，战争中的战争被归并进法国人与殖民部队之间战争的记述，很少（如果有的话）作为一个独立的叙述被详细展开。在这个意义上，它确实从未构成一个完整的序列，从未成为对任何一件“事情”的逐项实况记述。毋宁说，它的构成事件是作为其他记述的边缘子部分被提取的，而桑苏西本人的生与死又是这些子部分中更小的片段。为了重新发现桑苏西上校，使他成为海地建国故事中一个不可忽略的人物，我选择增加一节，在革命的编年概述之后，把他的故事重塑为一个独立的记述。这是一个基于可行程序和对读者知识评估的选择。那个选择承认了权力，但也引入了某种异议，因为它把战争中的战争确立为一个历史主题。

en: To be sure, I could have highlighted the figure of the Colonel in a different way. But I had to resort to a procedure of emphasis based on both content and form in order to reach my final goal, that of suggesting new significance to both the Haitian Revolution and to the Colonel’s life. I could not leave to chance the transformation of some silences into mentions or the possibility that mentions alone would add retrospective significance. In short, this unearthing of Sans Souci required extra labor not so much in the production of new facts but in their transformation into a new narrative.
zh: 诚然，我本可以用另一种方式突出上校的形象。但我不得不诉诸一种基于内容与形式两方面的强调程序，才能达到我的最终目标：为海地革命和上校的一生提示新的意义。我不能把某些沉默向提及的转化交给偶然，也不能指望仅凭提及就自然会增添回溯赋予的意义。简言之，这次重新发现桑苏西的工作所需要的额外劳动，与其说在于生产新事实，不如说在于把它们转化为一个新的叙述。

en: Silences Within Silences
zh: 沉默之中的沉默

en: The unearthing of silences, and the historian’s subsequent emphasis on the retrospective significance of hitherto neglected events, requires not only extra labor at the archives—whether or not one uses primary sources—but also a project linked to an interpretation. This is so because the combined silences accrued through the first three steps of the process of historical production intermesh and solidify at the fourth and final moment when retrospective significance itself is produced. To call this moment “final” does not suggest that it follows the chronological disappearance of the actors. Retrospective significance can be created by the actors themselves, as a past within their past, or as a future within their present. Henry I killed Sans Souci twice: first, literally, during their last meeting; second, symbolically, by naming his most famous palace Sans Souci. This killing in history was as much for his benefit as it was for our wonder. It erased Sans Souci from Christophe’s own past, and it erased him from his future, what has become the historians’ present. It did not erase Sans Souci from Christophe’s memory or even from the sources. Historian Hénock Trouillot, one of the few Haitians to emphasize the similarity between the two names, suggests that Christophe may even have wanted to perpetuate the memory of his enemy as the most formidable one he defeated. In other words, the silencing of Sans Souci could be read as an engraving of Christophe himself, the ultimate victor over all mortal enemies and over death itself:
zh: 对沉默的发掘，以及历史学家随后对此前被忽视事件的回溯性意义的强调，不仅需要在档案中付出额外劳动——无论是否使用第一手史料——还需要一个与某种解释相联系的研究计划。之所以如此，是因为历史生产过程前三个步骤积累起来的种种沉默相互交织，在第四个也是最后一个时刻——回溯性意义本身被生产的时刻——固化下来。把这个时刻称为“最后的”，并不意味着它发生在行动者按时间顺序消失之后。回溯性意义可以由行动者自己创造，作为他们过去之中的一个过去，或他们现在之中的一个未来。亨利一世杀了桑苏西两次：第一次是字面意义上的，在他们最后一次会面时；第二次是象征意义上的，通过把他最著名的宫殿命名为无忧宫。这次在历史中的杀戮，既是为了他自己的利益，也是为了让我们惊叹。它把桑苏西从克里斯托夫自己的过去中抹去，也把他从克里斯托夫的未来——也就是如今已成为历史学家的现在——中抹去。它没有把桑苏西从克里斯托夫的记忆中抹去，甚至没有从史料中抹去。历史学家埃诺克·特鲁约是少数强调两个名字相似之处的海地人之一，他提示，克里斯托夫甚至可能想让他这个敌人的记忆永存，作为他所击败的最可怕的敌人。换句话说，使桑苏西归于沉默，可以被读作对克里斯托夫本人的铭刻——他是战胜一切凡间敌人、乃至战胜死亡本身的终极胜利者：

en: In erecting Sans Souci at the foothills of Milot, did Christophe want to prove how solidly his power was implanted in this soil? Or else, was he dominated by a more obscure thought? For a legend reports that a diviner foretold Christophe that he would die by the hand of a Congo. Then, superstitious as he was, having satisfied his propensity for magic, did he believe that in erecting this town he could defy destiny?… We do not know.
zh: 克里斯托夫在米洛特山麓兴建无忧宫，是想证明他的权力在这片土地上扎根多么牢固吗？抑或，他是被一种更晦暗的念头所支配？因为有一则传说记载，一位占卜者曾预言克里斯托夫将死于一个刚果人之手。那么，像他这样迷信的人，在满足了自己对魔法的偏好之后，是否相信兴建这座城镇就能对抗命运？……我们不知道。

en: The suggestion is not far-fetched. That Christophe deemed himself one notch above most mortals was well known even in his lifetime. Further, his reliance on transformative rituals, his desire to control both humans and death itself are epitomized in his last moments. Having engaged unsuccessfully in various rituals to restore his failing health and knowing that he had lost the personal magnetism that made his contemporaries tremble at his sight, a paralyzed Christophe shot himself, reportedly with a silver bullet, before a growing crowd of insurgents reached Sans Souci. Whether that bullet was meant to save him from a Congo, as such, we do not know.
zh: 这个提示并非牵强。克里斯托夫自认高出大多数凡人一等，这在他生前就广为人知。再者，他对转化仪式的依赖、他想控制人类乃至死亡本身的欲望，在他生命的最后时刻得到了集中体现。在尝试各种仪式恢复日渐衰败的健康而未果之后，在知道自己已失去那种令同时代人一见他就发抖的个人威势之后，瘫痪的克里斯托夫开枪自尽，据说是用一颗银弹，赶在越来越多的起义者抵达无忧宫之前。那颗子弹是否正是为了让他免于死在一个刚果人手中，我们不知道。

en: But we know that the silencing was effective, that Sans Souci’s life and death have been endowed with only marginal retrospective significance while neither Christophe’s apologists nor his detractors fail to mention the king’s thirst for glory and the extent to which he achieved it in his lifetime and thereafter. The legend of the diviner may one day be transformed into fact. But Trouillot’s references to superstition notwithstanding, the real magic remains this dual production of a highly significant mention of glory and an equally significant silence. Christophe indeed defied the future with this silencing.
zh: 但我们知道沉默化是有效的：桑苏西的生与死只被赋予了边缘性的回溯性意义，而克里斯托夫的辩护者和贬损者都无一例外地提及这位国王对荣耀的渴求，以及他在生前身后实现这种渴求的程度。占卜者的传说也许有一天会被转化为事实。但尽管特鲁约提到了迷信，真正的魔法仍然是这种双重生产：一个高度重要的关于荣耀的提及，和一个同样重要的沉默。克里斯托夫确实以这次沉默化对抗了未来。

en: For silencing here is an erasure more effective than the absence or failure of memory, whether faked or genuine.

French general Pamphile de Lacroix had no particular reason to take publicly the side of either man at the time that he wrote his memoirs. He knew them both. His own life intersected with theirs in ways that usually inscribe events in memory: they were both his enemies and his subalterns at different times in a foreign war about which he was half-convinced and ended up losing. He is the only human being we know to have left records of a conversation with Christophe about Colonel Sans Souci. That sixty pages after he reports this conversation, de Lacroix mentions by name the favorite palace of Henry I without commenting on the connection between that name and the Colonel’s patronym testifies to the effectiveness of Christophe’s silencing.
zh: 因为这里的沉默化是一种抹除，比记忆的缺失或失效——无论假装还是真实——更有效。

法国将军庞菲尔·德拉克鲁瓦在撰写回忆录时，没有特别的理由公开站在两人中任何一边。他两人都认识。他自己的生命与他们的生命以通常会把事件铭刻进记忆的方式相交：在一场他半信半疑、最终以失败告终的异国战争中，他们先后既是他的敌人，又是他的下属。他是我们所知的唯一留下与克里斯托夫谈论桑苏西上校的记录的人。在报告这次谈话六十页之后，德拉克鲁瓦点名提到亨利一世最钟爱的宫殿，却没有评论那个名字与上校姓氏之间的联系——这证明了克里斯托夫沉默化的有效性。

en: Indeed, de Lacroix’s silence typifies an obliteration that may have gone beyond Christophe’s wishes. For in many non-Haitian circles, the disappearance of Sans Souci the man tied the entire significance of the palace at Milot to Sans Souci–Potsdam. Jonathan Brown, the physician from New Hampshire who visited Haiti a decade after Christophe’s death and failed to note the connection between the Colonel and the palace, wrote: “[Christophe] was particularly delighted with history, of which his knowledge was extensive and accurate; and Frederick the Great of Prussia was a personage with whom above all others he was captivated, the name of Sans Souci having been borrowed from Potsdam.”
zh: 的确，德拉克鲁瓦的沉默典型地体现了一种可能超出克里斯托夫意愿的湮灭。因为在许多非海地圈子里，桑苏西这个人的消失，把米洛特宫的全部意义都系在了波茨坦无忧宫上。来自新罕布什尔州的医生乔纳森·布朗在克里斯托夫死后十年访问海地，没有注意到上校与宫殿之间的联系，他写道：“〔克里斯托夫〕尤其喜爱历史，他的历史知识广博而准确；普鲁士的腓特烈大帝是他最为着迷的人物，无忧宫这个名字就是从波茨坦借来的。”

en: The excerpt from Brown is one of the earliest written mentions of a relationship between the two palaces and the most likely source for subsequent writers in the English language. The only reference to Potsdam prior to Brown in the corpus covered here is buried in a diatribe against Christophe by Haitian writer and politician Hérard Dumesle. Dumesle does not say that the Milot palace was designed or named after Potsdam. Rather, he emphasizes a fundamental contradiction between what he perceives as Frederick’s love of justice and Christophe’s tyranny.

Elsewhere in the book, Dumesle also compares Christophe with Nero and Caligula. He derides Christophe’s ceremonial corps of amazons who, in his view, were much less graceful than the real amazons of pre-conquest South America. In short, as mentioned by Dumesle, the connection between Potsdam and Milot is purely rhetorical. Has history turned this rhetoric into a source? Hubert Cole, who wrote an important biography of Christophe, expands on the theme of German influence on Haitian architecture of the time and claims that “German engineers” built the Citadel. Cole, like Brown, does not cite sources for his suggestions.
zh: 布朗的这段摘录，是关于两座宫殿之间关系的最早文字提及之一，也是后续英语作家最可能的来源。在这里考察的这批文献中，布朗之前唯一提到波茨坦的地方，埋在海地作家兼政治家埃拉尔·迪梅勒一篇抨击克里斯托夫的文章里。迪梅勒并没有说米洛特宫是仿照波茨坦设计或命名的。毋宁说，他强调的是他所认为的腓特烈对正义的热爱与克里斯托夫的暴政之间的根本矛盾。
在书中别处，迪梅勒还把克里斯托夫比作尼禄和卡利古拉。他嘲笑克里斯托夫的仪仗亚马逊女兵队，在他看来，她们远不如征服前南美洲真正的亚马逊人优雅。简言之，在迪梅勒那里，波茨坦与米洛特之间的联系纯粹是修辞性的。历史是否把这种修辞变成了史料？写过一部重要的克里斯托夫传记的休伯特·科尔，扩展了德国影响当时海地建筑这一主题，声称“德国工程师”建造了城堡。科尔和布朗一样，没有为他的说法引用来源。

en: Implicitly contradicting Brown and Cole, Haitian historian Vergniaud Leconte credits Christophe’s military engineer, Henri Barré, for the design of the Citadel and one Chéri Warloppe for the design and building of Sans Souci.

Leconte examined most writings then available about Christophe and claimed to have used new documents as well as oral sources, but except for locating Warloppe’s grave in a cemetery in northern Haiti, he does not tie his data to specific archives or sources. Leconte does not allude to any German influence. Explicitly rejecting such influence, Haitian architect Patrick Delatour, who is involved in the restoration of the palace, insists upon viewing it within Christophe’s larger project of building a royal town. For Delatour (personal communications), the foreign association—if any—is that of French urban planning at the turn of the century. Did someone dream of the German connection?
zh: 海地历史学家韦尔尼奥·勒孔特把城堡的设计归于克里斯托夫的军事工程师亨利·巴雷，把无忧宫的设计与建造归于一个名叫谢里·瓦洛普的人，这与布朗和科尔的说法隐然相悖。

勒孔特查考了当时可得的大多数关于克里斯托夫的著述，声称使用了新文献和口述来源，但除了在海地北部一处墓地找到瓦洛普的坟墓之外，他并没有把他的资料与具体档案或史料挂钩。勒孔特没有暗示任何德国影响。参与宫殿修复的海地建筑师帕特里克·德拉图尔明确否认曾有这种影响，坚持在克里斯托夫建造皇家城镇的更大规划中看待这座宫殿。对德拉图尔来说（私人交流），外国的关联——如果有的话——是世纪之交的法国城市规划。难道德国关联是某人梦想出来的吗？

en: There were German—and other European—residents in Christophe’s kingdom. There were Haitians fluent in German—and in other European languages—at the king’s personal service.

Moreover, Christophe did hire German military engineers to strengthen the defenses of his kingdom. Charles Mackenzie, the British consul in Haiti and a self-avowed spy, describes the case of two of these Germans whom Christophe jailed in order to prevent them from divulging military secrets. Yet Mackenzie, who visited and described Sans Souci less than ten years after Christophe’s death, does not connect the two palaces.
zh: 克里斯托夫的王国里有德国人及来自欧洲其他地方的居民。有精通德语——以及其他欧洲语言——的海地人在国王身边效力。
再者，克里斯托夫确实雇用德国军事工程师来加强王国的防务。英国驻海地领事、自认的间谍查尔斯·麦肯齐描述了其中两名德国人的遭遇：克里斯托夫把他们投入监狱，以防他们泄露军事机密。然而，在克里斯托夫死后不到十年就访问并描述无忧宫的麦肯齐，并没有把两座宫殿联系起来。

en: Still, given what we know of Henry I, and given the presence of German military architects in his kingdom, it is more than probable that he was aware of Potsdam’s existence and that he knew what it looked like. That Frederick contributed to the design of Sans Souci–Potsdam, wrote poetry, received in his palace celebrities of his time, men like Johann Sebastian Bach and Voltaire—also suggest an example that could have inspired Christophe. Henry I indeed supervised personally the construction of Sans Souci–Milot and maintained there the closest Haitian equivalent to an intellectual salon, thus reproducing, knowingly or not, aspects of the dream of Potsdam. None of this authenticates a strong Potsdam connection. Having compared numerous images of the two palaces, which include sketches of Sans Souci before 1842, I find that they betray some vague similarities both in general layout and in some details (the cupola of the church, the front arcades). But I will immediately confess that my amateurish associations require at least a suspicion of influence. How grounded is such a suspicion?
zh: 不过，鉴于我们对亨利一世的了解，鉴于他的王国里有德国军事建筑师，他很可能知道波茨坦的存在，也知道它是什么样子。腓特烈曾参与波茨坦无忧宫的设计、写诗、在宫中接待他那个时代的名人，如约翰·塞巴斯蒂安·巴赫和伏尔泰——这也提示了一个可能启发克里斯托夫的榜样。亨利一世确实亲自监督米洛特无忧宫的建造，并在那里维持了海地最像知识分子沙龙的聚会，从而有意无意地再现了波茨坦之梦的某些方面。这一切还不足以证实波茨坦有过显著影响。我比较过两座宫殿的众多图像，包括1842年以前的无忧宫素描，发现它们在总体布局和一些细节上（教堂的穹顶、正面的拱廊）流露出某种模糊的相似。但我要立即承认，我的业余联想至少得先假定米洛特可能受过波茨坦的影响。这个猜测有多少根据？

en: The strongest evidence against a strong Potsdam connection is yet another silence. Austro-German geographer Karl Ritter, a seasoned traveler and a keen observer of peoples and places, visited Sans Souci eight days after Christophe’s death. Ritter climbed upon a hill and drew a picture of the palace. His text describes in detail a building that was “built entirely according to European taste” and emphasizes such features as Christophe’s bathroom and the “European” plants in the garden.
Indeed, the word “European” returns many times in the written description, but nowhere is there the suggestion of an affinity between Christophe’s residence and that of Frederick.
zh: 反驳波茨坦曾有显著影响的最有力证据，是又一个沉默。奥地利—德国地理学家卡尔·里特是一位经验丰富的旅行家、对民族与地方的敏锐观察者，他在克里斯托夫死后八天访问了无忧宫。里特登上一座山丘，画下了宫殿的图。他的文字详细描述了一座“完全按照欧洲趣味建造”的建筑，强调诸如克里斯托夫的浴室和花园里“欧洲的”植物之类的特征。
的确，“欧洲的”一词在文字描述中多次出现，但没有任何地方暗示克里斯托夫的居所与腓特烈的居所之间有亲缘关系。

en: Ritter had the benefit of both immediacy and hindsight. Most resident foreigners had been kept away from the road to the Citadel and, therefore, from Sans Souci during Christophe’s tenure. A few days after the king’s suicide, some European residents rushed to discover by themselves Christophe’s two most famous constructions. Ritter joined that party. Thus, he visited the palace in the company of other whites at a time when Sans Souci “triggered so much interest” among the few white residents of Haiti that “every white had to talk about it.”
zh: 里特既能及时亲历，又有日后回看所见的优势。克里斯托夫在位期间，大多数侨居外国人都被挡在通往城堡的道路之外，因而也被挡在无忧宫之外。国王自杀几天后，一些欧洲居民急于亲自去发现克里斯托夫最著名的两座建筑。里特加入了那一行人。于是，他在其他白人的陪同下参观了宫殿，当时无忧宫在海地为数不多的白人居民中“激起了如此大的兴趣”，以至于“每个白人都不得不谈论它”。

en: Ritter does not report these conversations but one can presume that he took them into consideration while writing his text. At the same time, since that text was published much later, indeed after that of Dumesle and that of Mackenzie, Ritter could have picked up from either of these two writers hints to a German connection. Yet Ritter never alludes to a specifically “German” or “Prussian” influence on Sans Souci–Milot.

Either he never heard of it, even from fellow German speakers residing in Haiti, or he thought it inconsequential both then and later. How interesting, in light of this silence, that later writers gave Potsdam so much retrospective significance.
zh: 里特没有记录这些谈话，但可以推定他在撰写文字时把它们考虑在内。同时，由于那份文字出版得晚得多——确实在迪梅勒和麦肯齐的文字之后——里特本可以从这两位作家中的任何一位那里拾取关于德国关联的暗示。然而里特从未暗示对米洛特无忧宫有任何专门的“德国”或“普鲁士”影响。
要么他从未听说过这种影响，甚至从侨居海地的德语同胞那里也没听说；要么他当时和后来都认为它无关紧要。鉴于这一沉默，后来的作家赋予波茨坦如此多的回溯性意义，是多么有趣。

en: Hubert Cole is one of the few writers to have noted explicitly the connection between Potsdam, Milot, and Sans Souci the man, whom he identifies as a major-general. But he depreciates the link between the latter two and makes Potsdam pivotal. Cole spends a single sentence on the three faces of Sans Souci to produce a quite eloquent silence: “Here, at the foot of the Pic de la Ferrière, guarded by the fortress that he called Citadel-Henry, he built Sans-Souci, naming it out of admiration for Frederick the Great and despite the fact that it was also the name of the bitter enemy whom he had murdered.”
zh: 休伯特·科尔是少数明确注意到两座无忧宫与桑苏西这个人之间联系的作家之一，他把后者认作一名少将。但他贬低后两者之间的联系，使波茨坦成为枢纽。科尔只用一句话处理“无忧”的三副面孔，制造了一个相当雄辩的沉默：“在这里，在拉费里埃峰（Pic de la Ferrière）脚下，在他称为亨利城堡的要塞守卫下，他建造了无忧宫，命名是出于对腓特烈大帝的仰慕，尽管那也是他谋杀的死敌的名字。”

en: For Cole, the coincidence between Sans Souci–Milot and Sans Souci the man was an accident that the king easily bypassed. The Colonel had no symbolic significance (I am aware of being redundant in phrasing it this way), only a factual one. In retrospect, only Sans Souci–Potsdam mattered, though Cole does not say why it should matter so much. In so stressing Potsdam, Cole not only silences the Colonel, he also denies Christophe’s own attempt to silence Sans Souci the man. Cole’s silencing thus produces a Christophe who is a remorseless murderer, a tasteless potentate, a bare mimic of Frederick, a man who consumes his victim and appropriates his war name, not through a ritual of reckoning but by gross inadvertence.
zh: 对科尔来说，米洛特的无忧宫与桑苏西同名这件事，是国王轻易绕过的一个偶然。上校没有象征意义（我意识到这样措辞是冗余的），只有事实意义。回溯来看，只有波茨坦无忧宫才要紧，尽管科尔没有说它为什么应该如此要紧。如此强调波茨坦，科尔不仅使上校沉默，也否认了克里斯托夫本人使桑苏西这个人沉默的企图。于是，科尔的沉默化生产出一个这样的克里斯托夫：一个毫无悔意的谋杀者，一个趣味低劣的权贵，一个腓特烈的拙劣模仿者，一个吞噬受害者、据用其战时的名字的人——不是通过清算仪式，而是出于严重的疏忽。

en: Such a picture is not convincing. A 1786 map of northern Saint-Domingue shows the main Grand Pré plantation to be adjacent to the Millot [
] plantation.

Christophe used both places as headquarters. Given the size of the palace and its dependencies, the royal domain may have run over part of Grand Pré. In other words, Christophe built Sans Souci, the palace, a few yards away from—if not exactly—where he killed Sans Souci, the man. Coincidence and inadvertence seem quite improbable. More likely, the king was engaged in a transformative ritual to absorb his old enemy.
zh: 这样一幅图景不能令人信服。一幅1786年的圣多明各北部地图显示，大普雷主种植园与米洛特（原文 Millot，当作 Milot）种植园相邻。
克里斯托夫把两处都用作司令部。考虑到宫殿及其附属建筑的规模，皇家领地可能已延伸到大普雷种植园的一部分。换句话说，克里斯托夫建造无忧宫这座宫殿的地方，距他杀死桑苏西的地方只有几码远——如果不是恰恰就在那里的话。巧合与疏忽似乎极不可能。更可能的是，国王正在进行一种吸收旧敌的转化仪式。

en: Dahoman oral history reports that the country was founded by Tacoodonou after a successful war against Da, the ruler of Abomey. Tacoodonou “put Da to death by cutting open his belly, and placed his body under the foundation of a palace that he built in Abomey, as a memorial of his victory; which he called Dahomy, from Da the unfortunate victim, and Homy his belly: that is a house built in Da’s belly.”

The elements of the Sans Souci plot are there: the war, the killing, the building of a palace, and the naming of it after the dead enemy. Chances are that Christophe knew this story. He praised Dahomans as great warriors. He bought or recruited four thousand blacks—many of whom were reportedly from Dahomey—to bolster his army. A hundred and fifty of his Royal-Dahomets, based at Sans Souci, formed his cherished cadet troop.
In light of this, the emphasis on Potsdam by non-Haitian historians, which deprives the Colonel’s death of any significance, is also an act of silencing.
zh: 达荷美口述历史记载，这个国家是塔科多努在对阿波美统治者达发动一场成功的战争之后建立的。塔科多努“剖开达的肚子把他杀死，把他的尸体放在他在阿波美建造的一座宫殿的地基之下，作为他胜利的纪念；他把这座宫殿称为达荷美（Dahomy），取自达——那个不幸的受害者——和霍米（Homy，他的肚子）：也就是说，一座建在达肚子里的房子。”
桑苏西与无忧宫故事中的要素都在这里：战争、杀戮、建造宫殿、以死去的敌人为之命名。克里斯托夫很可能知道这个故事。他称赞达荷美人是伟大的战士。他购买或招募了四千名黑人——据说其中许多来自达荷美——来充实他的军队。他的一百五十名皇家达荷美卫队（Royal-Dahomets）驻扎在无忧宫，组成他珍爱的士官生部队。
有鉴于此，非海地历史学家对波茨坦的强调——它剥夺了上校之死的任何意义——也是一种沉默化行为。

en: The Defeat of the Barbarians
zh: “野蛮人”的败北

en: For Haitians, the silencing is elsewhere. To start with, Potsdam is not even a matter of fact. When I raised the issue of the influence of the German palace on the construction of Sans Souci, most of my Haitian interlocutors acknowledged ignorance. Some historians conceded that they had “heard of it,” but the connection was never taken seriously. In that sense, Haitian historians are playing by the rules of the Western guild: there is no irrefutable evidence of a connection between Milot and Potsdam. But for most Haitians (most urbanites at least), the silencing goes way beyond this mere matter of fact. The literate Haitians with whom I raised the Potsdam connection did not simply question the evidence. Rather, the attitude was that, even if proven, this “fact” itself did not much matter. Just as the Colonel’s name and murder—of which they are well aware—does not much matter.
zh: 对海地人来说，沉默化在别处。首先，波茨坦的影响甚至够不上一个公认的事实。当我提出德国宫殿对无忧宫建造的影响这一问题时，我的大多数海地对话者都承认不知情。一些历史学家承认他们“听说过”，但这种联系从未被认真对待。在这个意义上，海地历史学家是在按西方行会的规则行事：没有无可辩驳的证据表明米洛特与波茨坦之间存在联系。但对大多数海地人（至少大多数城市居民）来说，沉默化远远超出了这个单纯的事实问题。与我谈起波茨坦关联的那些识字的海地人，并不只是质疑证据。毋宁说，他们的态度是：即便得到证明，这个“事实”本身也无关紧要。正如上校的名字和他的被谋杀——他们对此心知肚明——也无关紧要。

en: For the Haitian urban elites, only Milot counts, and two of the faces of Sans Souci are ghosts that are best left undisturbed. The Colonel is for them the epitome of the war within the war, an episode that, until recently, they have denied, any retrospective significance. This fratricide sequence is the only blemish in the glorious epic of their ancestors’ victory against France, the only shameful page in the history of the sole successful slave revolution in the annals of humankind. Thus, understandably, it is the one page they would have written otherwise if history depended only on the wishes of the narrator. And indeed, they tried to rewrite it as much as they could. For most writers sympathetic to the cause of freedom, Haitians and foreigners alike, the war within the war is an amalgam of unhappy incidents that pitted the black Jacobins, Creole slaves and freedmen alike, against hordes of uneducated “Congos,” African-born slaves, Bossale men with strange surnames, like Sans Souci, Makaya, Sylla, Mavougou, Lamour de la Rance, Petit-Noël Prieur (or Prière), Va-Malheureux, Macaque, Alaou, Coco, Sanglaou—slave names quite distinguishable from the French sounding ones of Jean-Jacques Dessalines, Alexandre Pétion, Henry Christophe, Augustin Clervaux, and the like.
zh: 对海地城市精英来说，只有米洛特才算数，“无忧”的三副面孔中有两副是最好别去惊动的幽灵。上校对他们来说是战争中的战争的缩影，是一个直到不久之前他们一直否认有任何回溯性意义的插曲。这段同室操戈的序列，是他们的祖先战胜法国的光荣史诗中唯一的污点，是人类编年史上唯一成功的奴隶革命的历史中唯一可耻的一页。因此，可以理解，如果历史只取决于叙述者的愿望，这正是他们会以另一种方式书写的一页。而事实上，他们也确实尽其所能地试图重写它。对大多数同情自由事业的作家——无论海地人还是外国人——来说，战争中的战争是一堆不幸事件的混合体，这些事件让黑人雅各宾派——无论是克里奥尔奴隶还是自由民——与成群未受教育的“刚果人”对立，后者是非洲出生的奴隶，是带着奇怪姓氏的博萨尔人，如桑苏西、马卡亚、西拉、马武古、拉穆尔·德·拉朗斯、珀蒂-诺埃尔·普里厄尔（或普里耶尔）、瓦-马勒勒、马卡克、阿拉乌、科科、桑格劳——这些奴隶名字，与让-雅克·德萨利纳、亚历山大·佩蒂翁、亨利·克里斯托夫、奥古斯丁·克莱尔沃之类法国味十足的名字截然不同。

en: That many of these Congos were early leaders of the 1791 uprising, that a few had become bona fide officers of Louverture’s army, that all were staunch defenders of the cause of freedom have been passed over. The military experience gathered in Africa during the Congo civil wars, which may have been crucial to the slave revolution, is a non-issue in Haiti.

Not just because few Haitians are intimate with African history, but because Haitian historians (like everyone else) long assumed that victorious strategies could only come from the Europeans or the most Europeanized slaves. Words like Congo and Bossale carry negative connotations in the Caribbean today. Never mind that Haiti was born with a majority of Bossales. As the Auguste brothers have recently noted, no one wondered how the label “Congo” came to describe a purported political minority at a time when the bulk of the population was certainly African-born and probably from the Congo region.
zh: 这些刚果人中有许多是1791年起义的早期领袖，有几位已成为卢维杜尔军队中名副其实的军官，所有人都是自由事业的坚定捍卫者——这些都被略过了。在刚果内战期间于非洲积累的军事经验，可能对奴隶革命至关重要，在海地却很少有人当成一个问题来讨论。
这不仅因为很少有海地人熟悉非洲历史，也因为海地历史学家（和所有人一样）长期假定，制胜的战略只能来自欧洲人或最欧化的奴隶。刚果和博萨尔之类的词，今天在加勒比带有负面含义。尽管海地诞生时博萨尔人占人口多数，也无人在意。正如奥古斯特兄弟最近指出的，没有人追问过：在人口主体肯定是非洲出生、而且很可能来自刚果地区的时候，“刚果”这个标签怎么会用来描述一个所谓的政治少数派。

en: Jean-Baptiste Sans Souci is the Congo par excellence. He was the most renowned of the African rebels and the most effective from the point of view of both French and “colonial” higher ranks. He is a ghost that most Haitian historians—urban, literate, French speakers, as they all are—would rather lay to rest. “Mulatto” historian Beaubrun Ardouin, who helped launch Haitian historiography on a modern path, and whose thousands of pages have been pruned, acclaimed, plagiarized, and contested, is known for his hatred of Christophe and his harsh criticism of the dark-skinned heroes of Haitian independence. Yet, when it came to Sans Souci, Ardouin the “mulatto” took the black Creole’s side. Describing a meeting during the negotiations over the leadership in which a “courageous,” “energetic,” “distinguished,” “intelligent” and (suddenly) “good-looking” Christophe used his legendary magnetism to influence Sans Souci, Ardouin writes:
zh: 让-巴蒂斯特·桑苏西是典型的刚果人。他是非洲叛军中最著名的一位，在法国和“殖民”双方高层看来也是最有战斗力的一位。他是一个幽灵，大多数海地历史学家——他们全都是城市居民、识字者、法语使用者——宁愿让他安息。“穆拉托”历史学家博布伦·阿尔杜安帮助海地史学走上现代道路，他的数千页著作被人删节、赞誉、剽窃和争论，他以憎恨克里斯托夫、严厉批评海地独立运动中肤色黝黑的英雄而闻名。然而，一涉及桑苏西，“穆拉托”阿尔杜安却站到了克里斯托夫这个黑人克里奥尔人一边。他描述领导权谈判期间的一次会面，其中“勇敢的”、“精力充沛的”、“卓越的”、“聪明的”、（突然又）“相貌堂堂的”克里斯托夫凭他那早已传为传奇的个人威势震慑桑苏西，阿尔杜安写道：

en: [B]randishing his sword, (Christophe) moved toward (Sans Souci) and asked him to declare whether or not he did not acknowledge him as a général, his superior.… [S]ubjugated by the ascendance of a civilized man, and a former commander at that, the African told him: “General, what do you want to do?” “You are calling me general (replied Christophe); then, you do acknowledge me as your chief, since you are not a general yourself.” Sans Souci did not dare reply.… The Barbarian was defeated.
zh: “（克里斯托夫）挥舞着剑，走向（桑苏西），要他声明是否承认他是一位将军（général）、他的上级。……这个非洲人被一个文明人——而且是昔日的指挥官——的威势所慑服，对他说：‘将军，您想做什么？’‘你叫我将军（克里斯托夫回答）；那么，你就是承认我是你的首领，因为你自己不是将军。’桑苏西不敢回答。……这个野蛮人被击败了。”

en: Ardouin is quick to choose sides not only because he may feel culturally closer to Christophe, a “civilized man,” but also because, as a nationalist historian, he needs Christophe against Sans Souci.
zh: 阿尔杜安急于选边站，不仅因为他在文化上可能觉得与克里斯托夫这个“文明人”更亲近，也因为作为一个民族主义历史学家，他需要克里斯托夫来对抗桑苏西。

en: As the first independent modern state of the so-called Third World, Haiti experienced early all the trials of postcolonial nation-building. In contrast to the United States, the only postcolonial case before 1804, it did so within a context characterized by a dependent economy and freedom for all. Thus, while the elites’ claims to state control required, as elsewhere, the partial appropriation of the culture-history of the masses, they also required, perhaps more than elsewhere, the silencing of dissent. Both the silencing of dissent and the building of state institutions started with the Louverture regime whose closest equivalent in post-independent Haiti was Henry I’s kingdom. In short, Christophe’s fame as a builder, both figuratively and literally, and his reputation as a ruthless leader are two sides of the same coin. Ardouin, a political kingmaker in his own time, knows this. Both he and Christophe belong to the same elites that must control and normalize the aspirations of the barbarians.
zh: 作为所谓第三世界第一个独立的现代国家，海地很早就经历了后殖民民族国家建设的全部考验。与1804年之前唯一的后殖民案例美国不同，它是在一种依附性经济与全民自由并存的语境中经历这些考验的。因此，精英阶层对国家控制权的诉求，如同在别处一样，要求部分占用大众的文化—历史；同时也要求——也许比别处更甚——使异议沉默。使异议沉默与国家制度的建设，都始于卢维杜尔政权，而独立后的海地与之最接近的对应物，就是亨利一世的王国。简言之，克里斯托夫作为建设者——无论比喻意义还是字面意义——的名声，与他作为无情领袖的名声，是一枚硬币的两面。阿尔杜安在他那个时代是能左右政治领袖人选的人，他懂得这一点。他和克里斯托夫都属于同一个精英阶层，这个阶层必须控制并规训那些“野蛮人”的抱负。

en: Ardouin also needs Christophe against the French. In spite of the attributes that Ardouin abhors and that he finds elsewhere hard to reconcile with civilization, Christophe is part of the glory that Ardouin claims to be his past. Christophe beat the French; Sans Souci did not. Christophe erected these monuments to the honor of the black race, whereas Sans Souci, the African, nearly stalled the epic.
zh: 阿尔杜安还需要克里斯托夫来对抗法国人。尽管克里斯托夫具有阿尔杜安憎恶、在别处觉得难以与文明相容的那些特质，他仍是阿尔杜安宣称属于自己的过去的那份荣耀的一部分。克里斯托夫打败了法国人；桑苏西没有。克里斯托夫竖起这些纪念碑，为黑人种族增光；而桑苏西这个非洲人，却几乎让这部史诗停滞。

en: For Ardouin, as for many other Haitians, Sans Souci is an inconvenience inasmuch as the war within the war may prove to be a distraction from the main event of 1791–1804: the successful revolution that their ancestors launched against both slavery and colonialism and that the white world did its best to forget. Here, the silencing of Sans Souci the man and that of Sans Souci–Potsdam converge. They are silences of resistance, silences thrown against a superior silence, that which Western historiography has produced around the revolution of Saint-Domingue/Haiti. In the context of this silencing, which we explore in the next chapter, Potsdam remains a vague suggestion, the Colonel’s death is a mere matter of fact, while the crumbling walls of Milot still stand as a last defense against oblivion.
